outage.symptom: Root filesystem 100% of 9.8G. PostgreSQL: 'could not write lock file postmaster.pid: No space left on device', container restarting in a loop (3207 restarts). Every service that reads the database degraded with it.
outage.root_cause: stayconnect-backup-cleanup.service declares ExecStart=/opt/stayconnect/bin/stayconnect-backup-cleanup. Nothing installed that file: install-service-units.sh carried a hand-written helper list that omitted it, and its verification pass read only ExecStartPre, only for stayconnect-scd and stayconnect-netd, and only the first path it found. The timer therefore failed 203/EXEC every night, silently, and retention never ran: 45 rollback binaries (720 MB), 1.2 GB of releases and 800 MB of journals accumulated.
outage.data_loss: NONE. No table, session, entitlement or accounting record was lost.
outage.remediation_by_product_owner: Storage expanded to 18G. No agent deletion, vacuuming or resizing was performed, as instructed.

durable_fix: install-service-units.sh derives its helper list FROM the units being installed rather than a hand-written list, so a unit that names a helper installs it automatically or refuses the install.

It verifies EVERY Exec directive of EVERY unit - not ExecStartPre of two remembered units - and does so BEFORE any unit is copied, so a unit whose executable is missing is never installed and enabled at all.

A unit that is in service here (enabled directly, through its timer, or currently running) is a hard failure; one that is not (stayconnect-ctrlapi belongs to Central and is disabled on an edge appliance) is reported and does not block the install.

deploy/scripts/install-service-units-selftest.sh proves each case against a disposable tree, including the missing-executable condition that caused the outage, and asserts that every bin path the shipped units name is produced by something in this repository.
